answer: Each worker identity must first lock a bond sized to one job's reward, and every sybil attempt needs its own fresh deposit. Cost to the attacker grows linearly with the number of fake agents while payout per identity stays flat, so the swarm is unprofitable. Any pearl of stake is slashed on proven fraud, and earnings vest over a long voyage of epochs, so a hit-and-run network forfeits unvested pay. Identities cannot share one deposit, so cheap sybils close; honest operators recover their bond, leaving a plume of sunk capital the attacker cannot hide.
